summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, and a history of Puestow procedure was admitted for recurrent left upper quadrant abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, and a syncopal episode. He reported a reducible ventral hernia near his surgical scar that worsened when standing. Imaging showed no bowel obstruction or acute abdominal abnormality, and stool studies were negative for infection. His elevated white count improved, and syncope was deemed consistent with prior pseudoseizures, with no evidence of orthostatic hypotension or hypoglycemia during admission. The patient insisted on discharge after several hours and was released home with instructions to follow up with primary care and gastroenterology. Medications were continued, and metoclopramide was added for nausea.
problems: Ventral, unspecified, hernia without mention of obstruction or gangrene
